title: The Terminal of New Lagos
premise: Ansel Montrose navigates the freighter Vesper's Lament along the last open corridor between the Lagos Combine and the Meridian Fleet, two powers whose war is held off only by a treaty neither side believes in. When a derelict returns from deep space carrying its entire crew aged backward into childhood, Ansel recognizes one of the children as himself — a backup of his own mind, grown young again in stolen flesh. To keep the fleets from tearing each other apart over the discovery, he must sustain a lie about what happened aboard that ship, even as the child-Ansel remembers everything and both governments close in. In the end, Ansel sacrifices his identity — surrendering his name, his records, and his route to the boy — so that the truth can be buried, the peace can hold, and someone else can carry the life he no longer wants.
about_author: F. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports before turning those routes into fiction. They live between Accra and Lisbon and write at night, when the ports are quiet.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Ansel pilots the Vesper's Lament through the silent corridor separating the two fleets, establishing his routine, his loneliness, and the sealed hold where illegal mind-backups sleep in stasis. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: A power fluctuation wakes Ansel at night; he checks the backups and finds one pod's occupant dreaming audibly, murmuring coordinates only he knows. His engineer, Dara Okonjo, notices his fear but says nothing. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: creeping guilt.

chapters.title: Signal from Nowhere
chapters.summary: The Lament intercepts a distress beacon from a Meridian survey vessel, the Halcyon Reach, missing for eleven years. Command on both sides orders it ignored; Ansel, unable to resist, alters course. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: fatal curiosity.

chapters.title: The Ship Full of Children
chapters.summary: Boarding the Reach, Ansel and Dara find its crew aged backward — adults reduced to children with adult memories intact, including the captain, now eight years old, who salutes them. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: What the Boy Knows
chapters.summary: The child-captain, Idris Vane, describes a phenomenon called the Fold — a region where time runs backward — and mentions a passenger manifest name that stops Ansel cold: A. Montrose. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: recognition and terror.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Both governments demand custody of the Reach. Ansel reports the ship 'sterile and uninhabited,' buying time, while Dara begins secretly studying Idris's blood. POV: Ansel, shifting briefly to Dara. Emotional beat: the first deliberate lie.

chapters.title: The Combine's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Combine inspector Yewande Adeyemi boards under diplomatic pretext, probing Ansel's story with polite, surgical questions. He realizes she already suspects him. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: pressure tightening like a vise.

chapters.title: Meridian's Ghost Fleet
chapters.summary: A Meridian cruiser shadows the corridor; its commander, Halvorsen, transmits a private offer: hand over the Reach and be rewarded, refuse and be boarded. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: caught between two predators.

chapters.title: Memories Not Mine
chapters.summary: Idris, drawn to Ansel, recounts a memory of the hold of the Lament — a memory Ansel has never told anyone. The boy may be more than a copy; he may be the original, reversed. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: identity beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Dara's Discovery
chapters.summary: Dara confirms the reversed crew share genetic markers with living people across both fleets — the Fold doesn't copy people, it returns them. She urges Ansel to tell the truth; he refuses. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by conscience.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Yewande searches the Lament and finds the backup pods. Ansel talks his way past her by claiming they're treaty-sanctioned insurance — a lie that could hang him if either fleet checks. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: a liar at the edge of exposure.

chapters.title: Childhood, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Idris begins aging forward rapidly, days passing on his face by the hour, and begs Ansel to let him finish becoming whoever he'll become. Ansel sees his own future in the boy's hunger. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: tenderness inside urgency.

chapters.title: The Corridor Closes
chapters.summary: Both fleets declare the corridor a contested zone; the Lament is trapped between blockades with a ship full of reversing children aboard. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: claustrophobia, no way out.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Boarding
chapters.summary: Meridian marines storm the Lament. Ansel hides the children in the hold among the sleeping backups, and Halvorsen finds only pods — but takes Dara hostage as leverage. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: sacrifice forced early.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: To save Dara, Ansel offers Halvorsen the truth about the Fold — enough to start a war over immortality. Yewande intercepts the transmission and realizes his lie was holding the peace together all along. POV: Yewande. Emotional beat: the lie revealed as load-bearing.

chapters.title: What Ansel Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: years ago, Ansel discovered the Fold during an unauthorized deep-route run, erased the evidence, and made the backups to preserve what he'd found — and what he'd lost there. POV: Ansel (past). Emotional beat: understanding the man who lied.

chapters.title: Fleets in Formation
chapters.summary: Both armadas converge on the Reach's position. Idris, now nearly adult, finishes reversing and confronts Ansel: he remembers being the one who chose to erase everything, and he forgives him. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: mirror and mercy.

chapters.title: The Fold Opens
chapters.summary: The Reach's drive, still attuned to the Fold, tears open a temporal rift near the blockade line. Time stutters across both fleets — ships flicker older and younger — and panic spreads through every bridge. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: awe and chaos.

chapters.title: One Truth Between Armies
chapters.summary: At the climax, Ansel broadcasts the whole truth — the Fold, the reversals, his own erasures — betting that shared terror will do what treaties couldn't. Both fleets hold fire, staring into the rift together. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: confession as salvation.

chapters.title: The Handover
chapters.summary: To seal the truce, Ansel surrenders his identity: his records, his name, his route rights transferred to Idris, who will live the life forward that Ansel lived backward. Yewande certifies the transfer; Halvorsen withdraws. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Navigator, Unnamed
chapters.summary: Ansel, now legally nobody, walks the Reach's restored decks among the re-aged crew who don't know him. Dara chooses to stay with him anyway, calling him by no name at all. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: belonging without identity.

chapters.title: The Terminal of New Lagos
chapters.summary: Months later, a new navigator named Idris Montrose runs the corridor, while Ansel works the terminal docks under a labor alias, watching ships leave. The fleets talk again; the lie is dead and the peace lives. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
